title: अध्याय ६९

items.text:
आलोच्याज्ञापयेत्युक्ते ततो ज्ञातं मयापि तत् ।
ततो न दत्तवानर्घमहं तुभ्यं विधानतः ॥ ५४ ॥
items.tr:
ālocyājñāpayetyukte tato jñātaṃ mayāpi tat |
tato na dattavānarghamahaṃ tubhyaṃ vidhānataḥ || 54 ||

items.text:
सत्यं राजन् ! त्वमर्घार्हः कुले स्वायम्भुवस्य च ।
तथापि नार्घयोग्यं त्वां मन्यामो वयमुत्तमम् ॥ ५५ ॥
items.tr:
satyaṃ rājan ! tvamarghārhaḥ kule svāyambhuvasya ca |
tathāpi nārghayogyaṃ tvāṃ manyāmo vayamuttamam || 55 ||

items.text:
; राजोवाच
किं कृतं हि मया ब्रह्मन् ! ज्ञानादज्ञानतोऽपि वा ।
येन त्वत्तोर्ऽघमर्हामि नाहमभ्यागतश्चिरात् ॥ ५६ ॥
items.tr:
; rājovāca
kiṃ kṛtaṃ hi mayā brahman ! jñānādajñānato'pi vā |
yena tvattor'ghamarhāmi nāhamabhyāgataścirāt || 56 ||

items.text:
किं विस्मृतन्ते यत्पत्नी त्वया त्यक्ता च कानने ।
परित्यक्तस्तया सार्धं त्वया धर्मो नृपाखिलः ॥ ५७ ॥
items.tr:
kiṃ vismṛtante yatpatnī tvayā tyaktā ca kānane |
parityaktastayā sārdhaṃ tvayā dharmo nṛpākhilaḥ || 57 ||
items.speaker: ; ऋषिरुवाच

items.text:
पक्षेण कर्मणो हान्या प्रयात्यस्पर्शतां नरः ।
विण्मूत्रैर्वार्षिकी यस्य हानिस्ते नित्यकर्मणः ॥ ५८ ॥
items.tr:
pakṣeṇa karmaṇo hānyā prayātyasparśatāṃ naraḥ |
viṇmūtrairvārṣikī yasya hāniste nityakarmaṇaḥ || 58 ||

items.text:
पत्न्यानुकूलया भाव्यं यथाशीलेऽपि भर्तरि ।
दुः शीलापि तथा भार्या पोषणीया नरेश्वर ॥ ५९ ॥
items.tr:
patnyānukūlayā bhāvyaṃ yathāśīle'pi bhartari |
duḥ śīlāpi tathā bhāryā poṣaṇīyā nareśvara || 59 ||

items.text:
प्रतिकूला हि सा पत्नी तस्य विप्रस्य या हृता ।
तथापि धर्मकामोऽसौ त्वामुद्योतितवान् नृप ॥ ६० ॥
items.tr:
pratikūlā hi sā patnī tasya viprasya yā hṛtā |
tathāpi dharmakāmo'sau tvāmudyotitavān nṛpa || 60 ||

items.text:
चलतः स्थापयस्यन्यान् स्वधर्मेषु महीपते ।
त्वां स्वधर्माद्विचलितं कोऽपरः स्थापयिष्यति ॥ ६१ ॥
items.tr:
calataḥ sthāpayasyanyān svadharmeṣu mahīpate |
tvāṃ svadharmādvicalitaṃ ko'paraḥ sthāpayiṣyati || 61 ||

items.speaker: ; मार्कण्डेय उवाच
items.text:
विलक्ष्यः स महीपाल इत्युक्तस्तेन धीमता ।
तथेत्युक्त्वा च पप्रच्छ हृतां पत्नीं द्विजन्मनः ॥ ६२ ॥
items.tr:
vilakṣyaḥ sa mahīpāla ityuktastena dhīmatā |
tathetyuktvā ca papraccha hṛtāṃ patnīṃ dvijanmanaḥ || 62 ||

items.text:
भगवन् ! केन नीता सा पत्नी विप्रस्य कुत्र वा ।
अतीतानागतं वेत्ति जगत्यवितथं भवान् ॥ ६३ ॥
items.tr:
bhagavan ! kena nītā sā patnī viprasya kutra vā |
atītānāgataṃ vetti jagatyavitathaṃ bhavān || 63 ||

items.text:
तां जहाराद्रितनयो बलाको नाम राक्षसः ।
द्रक्ष्यसे चाद्य तां भूप ! उत्पलावतके वने ॥ ६४ ॥
items.tr:
tāṃ jahārādritanayo balāko nāma rākṣasaḥ |
drakṣyase cādya tāṃ bhūpa ! utpalāvatake vane || 64 ||
items.speaker: ; ऋषिरुवाच

items.text:
गच्छ संयोजयाशु त्वं भार्यया हि द्विजात्तमम् ।
मा पापास्पदतां यातु त्वमिवासौ दिने दिने ॥ ६५ ॥
items.tr:
gaccha saṃyojayāśu tvaṃ bhāryayā hi dvijāttamam |
mā pāpāspadatāṃ yātu tvamivāsau dine dine || 65 ||

en_summary: This chapter, part of the story of the Uttama Manu period, survives here only from its verse 53; the opening is missing and the first line is garbled. A sage who knows the past, present and future is speaking to King Uttama. He says that after thinking it over he understood the matter, and that is why he did not offer the king the guest water (arghya) in the proper way: the king is indeed worthy of it by his birth in the family of Svayambhuva, yet the sage does not consider him fit for it. The king asks what he has done, knowingly or unknowingly, to lose this honour, since he has come after a long time. The sage asks whether he has forgotten that he abandoned his wife in the forest, and with her gave up his whole dharma. A man who fails in his rites for a fortnight becomes untouchable, and the king has failed in his daily rites for a year. A wife should be agreeable to her husband whatever his character, and a husband must support his wife even if she is ill-behaved. The Brahmin whose wife was carried off also had a difficult wife, yet, wanting dharma, he came and urged the king to act. The king sets others back on their duty when they slip; who will set him back on his own? Ashamed, the king agrees and asks who took the Brahmin's wife and where she is. The sage says a rakshasa named Balaka, son of Adri, carried her off, and the king will see her today in the forest of Utpalavataka; he should go quickly and reunite the Brahmin with his wife, so that the Brahmin does not, like the king, become a place of sin day after day.
